tweet.text:
We eliminated 23 production failures in our multi-agent runtime this week and cut execution errors to zero.

Here is what broke in production and what we did.

When an agent crashes during parallel tool execution, developers assume it is a 
context window overflow 
or an LLM hallucination .

It was none of those things.

It was an unbatched assistant message in the provider's SSE stream.

When our model invoked two tools in one turn, the gateway recorded each tool call as a separate assistant message. On the next turn, consecutive assistant messages without intervening tool replies caused OpenRouter to drop the connection with an HTTP 502 error.

We batched the entire turn into a single assistant message before sending tool responses. All 23 failures disappeared.

Common belief: when a human operator rejects an agent's proposed action, you must abort the whole workflow. this is a wrong desing.

If an agent proposes sending a Slack update and drafting an email, rejecting the email should not destroy the Slack message.

Instead of killing the run, you have to prune the workflow. Cancel the rejected task, prune its downstream dependents, and let independent approved branches finish cleanly.

All in all: batch your parallel tool calls into a single message before sending them back to the provider, and prune rejected tasks instead of killing the entire workflow.
